neighbours.label: a famous name used as a TYPE for someone or something else (antonomasia: 'the Japanese Picasso', 'the Moses of her people', 'the Nielsen of radio', 'the Venice of the north'), on the name or the 'of' after it; the same names used literally stay quiet
fire: Fans call the young striker the Brazilian Messi.
Silicon Valley is often described as the Hollywood of tech.
The chef was hailed as the Mozart of pastry.
Locals say Lake Bled makes Slovenia the Switzerland of the Balkans.
Critics dubbed her the Hemingway of crime fiction.
The small app became the Uber of dog walking.
Many call Mumbai the New York of India.
He was known as the Einstein of his village.
quiet: Fans watched Messi score twice in Barcelona.
Hollywood studios released fewer films this year.
The orchestra played Mozart for the pastry chefs.
Critics reread Hemingway's novels every summer.
She ordered an Uber to the dog park.
Many flights from New York land in Mumbai.
neighbours.short: a famous name used as a type ('the Picasso of …')
neighbours.notes: A reader of the role-analogy 'of' unit L8/N106+ (drop 0.06). Probes: 'the Japanese Picasso' 0.79, 'the Moses of her people' 0.68, 'the Nielsen of radio' 0.94, 'the Serena Williams of chess' 0.84, 'the Venice of the north' 0.69, 'a modern-day Robin Hood' 0.28; the same names used literally 0.002-0.008.
